questions.q: Which two object types are Unity Catalog's 'container objects'?
options: Catalogs and schemas
Tables and views
Metastores and workspaces
Volumes and functions
questions.explain: Catalogs (containing schemas) and schemas (containing tables, views, volumes, and functions) are the only two container object types in Unity Catalog's model.

questions.q: If SELECT is granted on a schema today, does a table created in that schema next month inherit the grant?
options: Yes — privilege inheritance applies to all current and future child objects, automatically
No — a new GRANT is required for every new table
Only if the table is explicitly re-registered with the schema
Only if the grant is re-run manually after the table is created
questions.explain: Inheritance is forward-looking: a privilege granted on a container automatically applies to all current AND future children, with no new grant needed.

questions.q: What are USE CATALOG and USE SCHEMA, in Unity Catalog's permission model?
options: Usage privileges — prerequisites for reaching anything inside that container, regardless of other privileges held
Deprecated legacy privileges with no current effect
Privileges that only apply to account admins
Optional privileges that speed up query performance but aren't required for access
questions.explain: USE CATALOG and USE SCHEMA are usage privileges: without them on the relevant parent containers, even having SELECT on a table isn't enough to read it.

questions.q: Why can't a table owner alone grant someone access that reaches outside catalog/schema-approved boundaries?
options: Because only a catalog or schema's owner (or a MANAGE holder) can grant the USE CATALOG / USE SCHEMA privileges those boundaries depend on
Because table owners cannot run GRANT statements at all
Because Unity Catalog ignores all table-level grants automatically
Because table-level grants expire after 24 hours
questions.explain: A table owner handing out SELECT doesn't open any doors unless the catalog and schema owners already granted the usage privileges — this is a deliberate design to prevent lower-level owners from bypassing higher-level boundaries.

questions.q: How does holding MANAGE on a schema affect usage-privilege requirements?
options: It removes the USE SCHEMA requirement at that schema, but USE CATALOG on the parent catalog is still required
It removes every usage-privilege requirement everywhere in the metastore
It has no effect on usage-privilege requirements at all
It requires an additional USE SCHEMA grant on top of MANAGE, not a reduction
questions.explain: MANAGE reduces the usage-privilege requirement only at the level it's granted — MANAGE on a schema still requires USE CATALOG on the parent catalog, just not USE SCHEMA on that schema itself.
